title: Trigger-2 Canonical 46-Atom Split Manifest and Cross-Family Placeholder Namespace Reconciliation
summary: SUPERVISOR_INBOX.json flagged trigger2_canonical_tokenizer_abi_binding as a P1_BLOCKER after the B0-B6 cross-family consolidation pass found 168 distinct placeholder ABI_ACCEPTED_ORDINAL:NN ordinals in use across the candidate corpus (B0-B3: 15, B4: 80, B5: 93) against the course document's declared 46 real accepted atoms. claude-code-lead scoped the problem directly against generator source (no family ever shows more than ~24 atoms simultaneously in one row -- the 168-count is pure cross-episode ID bookkeeping, not a structural capacity conflict), found the actual 46 real atom NAMES already documented in-repo (research_entity/global/j-space/research/2026-08-26_TRIGGER2_ABI_SYMBOL_PRIOR_CONTEXTUAL_TOKEN_AUDIT_V1_GPT56SOL.json: A-Z, 0-9, and 10 words yes/no/true/false/maybe/unknown/if/then/not/and, 'or' rejected), and built tools/trigger2_canonical_atom_split_manifest_v1.py: a deterministic, stratified TRAIN_AND_VALIDATION(37)/HOLDOUT_FROZEN(9) split of the 46 names plus a remap_ordinal(family, ordinal, split_role) function, empirically verified against all 195 distinct placeholder ordinals actually used in the committed corpus (0 TRAIN/HOLDOUT crossings after excluding the known B4 decoy range; 1170 family x ordinal remap checks, 0 failures). This resolves the NAMESPACE/DESIGN half of the blocker without rewriting any already-committed family data. Later the same day a sibling agent (commit 8840389) ran the FIRST real tokenizer test against the actual pinned checkpoint inside clay-direct-dev: architecture claims matched exactly, all 46 atoms are single-token standalone-no-space, but all 10 digit atoms ('0'-'9') split into 2 tokens whenever preceded by a whitespace -- the common real-render case -- while letters and words stay single-token everywhere tested. This is a genuine, load-bearing caveat on this packet's own digit-atom assignment, incorporated here rather than left in a separate packet. TRIGGER2_ABI_CONTEXTUAL_RENDER_GATE/v1 still stays not fully closed: no atoms_index.json ingested, fix_mistral_regex variant untested, only 2 contextual templates probed.
open_questions: When exact atoms_index.json, tokenizer and renderer bytes become available, does rendering every committed placeholder occurrence through remap_ordinal() and then re-running each family's own leakage audit against the real-atom rendered bytes still pass cleanly, or do exact tokenizer boundary effects (subword splits, whitespace/punctuation interaction) reopen any check?

Is the ~80/20 TRAIN_AND_VALIDATION/HOLDOUT_FROZEN split ratio (matching blueprint_v2's own 12:3 donor ratio) the right choice once real per-atom accuracy data exists, or should it be revisited per H_T2_ABI_01's neutral-vs-language-bearing stratified comparison results?

Should the canonical manifest eventually replace each family's own placeholder atom_ref()/ATOM_POOL constants directly (a source-level rewrite) once real binding is authorized, or should remap_ordinal() remain a separate reconciliation layer applied only at final-render time?

Which digit-atom render rule should be adopted -- no-leading-space rendering everywhere (constrains template design) or accepting the fixed 2-token ('Ġ',digit) span as the digit stratum's target span (requires a render-gate rule change)? See H-T2ABI-003.
